Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Houston/Galveston TX
545 AM CDT Sun Jul 26 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Dangerous heat building this week with temperatures in the upper
  90s/100s and heat indices of 104-112F. Heat Advisories likely at
  times during the upcoming work week.

- Patchy fog possible during the early to mid-morning hours for at
  least the next few days.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1122 PM CDT Sat Jul 25 2026

To give y'all an idea of what's up ahead over the next several
days: today was the "coolest" day of the forecast period, and we 
had high temperatures in the low to mid 90s. The City of Houston 
has only had one day above 100 degrees so far this year...and we 
have pretty high confidence that we'll be adding onto that next 
week. The 596-598 dam mid-level high (AKA the heatdome) has nudged
a bit eastward from yesterday and is now centered just east of 
the Four Corners. It will continue to drift eastward going into 
Sunday and early next week, which will pair with 850mb 
temperatures increasing to above the 90th percentile and 
occasionally approaching the 99th percentile for most of the work 
week. That means triple digit heat is on the horizon...and we 
haven't even discussed the humidity part of it yet. 

South-southwesterly to southerly surface flow should keep dew points 
elevated (low to mid 70s) closer to the coast. Further inland, we 
should see dew points mixing down into the upper 60s to low 70s in 
the afternoons during the work week. The air temperatures will be 
high enough though that we'll still see heat indices peaking near or 
above the Heat Advisory threshold (greater than 108 degrees) at 
times next week. Decided to hold off on a Heat Advisory for Sunday 
since we won't see widespread locations reaching criteria...not 
entirely ruling out a few spots reaching criteria though. There 
won't be much relief overnight with low temperatures mainly in the 
upper 70s to low 80s. The atrocious humidity overnight will result 
in occasional rounds of patchy fog in the early to mid morning hours 
for at least the next few days. Sunday will feature a slight chance 
of rain even in the midst of increasing subsidence. It'll be a 
battle of increasing subsidence versus a team-up of daytime heating, 
the sea breeze, an embedded shortwave, and increased moisture just 
below the 75th percentile (~2.03"). Not quite as exciting as an 
endgame battle, but there's not much else to talk about other than 
the heat so we're watching with great interest! Destiny arrives all 
the same though, because most of us won't see a drop of rain over 
the next several days and will be left to deal with the sweltering 
heat. 

PW values decrease again closer to the 10th percentile (~1.36") 
through at least midweek, so rain chances will be slim to none for 
most of the work week. Towards the end of the work week, the 
heatdome begins to retreat westward a bit which may open the door 
for some isolated convection...but we're keeping that potential on 
the low side for now. Continuing to look towards next weekend for a 
return of more sufficient rain chances. Ensemble guidance (both GEFS 
and the Euro) have decent agreement on a surface low developing near 
the Red River towards the end of the work week. This coincides with 
the heatdome retreating westward and an upper level trough drifting 
through the eastern CONUS. Does this bring a weak frontal boundary 
in the vicinity of our area along with increasing moisture? I can't 
say yes...but I also can't say no. After what looks to be multiple 
100+ degree days in a row, I would gladly take some rain! 
Uncertainty is still fairly high with this, so we'll continue to 
monitor trends as the week progresses.

With heat indices expected to be near or above Heat Advisory 
criteria as early as Sunday, please keep heat safety at the top of 
your minds for any plans that you make (especially if outdoors). 
Know the signs of heat-related illnesses, stay hydrated (with 
water), take frequent breaks from the heat, wear loose/light-colored 
clothing and sunscreen, and ALWAYS ALWAYS ALWAYS LOOK before you 
LOCK your vehicle. Don't forget about your pets as well! If the 
ground is too hot for the palm of your hand, then it is too hot for 
their paws. 

Batiste

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAF Issuance)
Issued at 545 AM CDT Sun Jul 26 2026

A fcst of persistence for the most part. Like the past couple
days, we're seeing some intermittent, patchy MVFR vsby/cigs 
across parts of the area...mainly outside the metro terminals. 
These should lift by mid morning with VFR conditions generally 
prevailing for the remainder of the day until we do it all over 
again later tonight. We might see a few light shra dotting some 
of the coastal counties this morning. Some of the hires guidance 
has shown some consistency showing an isolated cell or two 
developing in the IAH/CXO areas between 22-01z, so threw in a 
PROB30 there. 47

A period of benign marine conditions continues with light to

prevailing over the next several days.

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Lake Charles LA
1225 PM CDT Sun Jul 26 2026

...New DISCUSSION, AVIATION, MARINE, FIRE WEATHER...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Dangerous heat this week with temperatures in the upper 90s to
  100s and heat indices of 106-110F. Heat Advisories are likely 
  at times next week.

- Later in the week, upper ridging begins to lose its control
  overhead, allowing temps to moderate slightly and rain chances 
  to return to the forecast
  

&&

.DISCUSSION...
(This evening through next Saturday)
Issued at 1217 PM CDT Sun Jul 26 2026

Hot weather will continue to be the main concern across the 
region. Aloft, ridging is centered over the Four Corners region 
and extends to the Gulf Coast. This is a fairly strong ridge for 
this July, with 500 mb heights over the CWA above the 
climatological 90th percentile. Persistent sinking air associated 
with this ridge will keep our skies clear and rain chances below 
10%. At the surface, high pressure is located in the eastern Gulf,
creating continuous but weak onshore flow. Dew points will slowly
increase, then plateau into the mid-70s inland and the upper 70s 
along the coast. With the clear skies daytime heating will help 
mix down some of the dry air limiting dew points. Temperatures 
will also steadily increase, with highs in the upper 90s and close
to triple digits for northern parts of the CWA. Heat index values
will approach the +108 criteria for a Heat Advisory each day 
during the work week, with the hottest days of the week looking 
like Tuesday and Wednesday. Even without heat advisories, make 
sure to stay hydrated and take plenty of breaks from the heat.


This pattern will remain stagnant for the next several days with
little change to our synoptic setup. We will start to see the
ridge begin to weaken and rebuild in the desert southwest. This
will allow for troughs to rotate around the ridge increasing our
rain chances for the end of the week. With the increase in rains
temperatures will decrease slightly back down into the mid 90s.

&&

.AVIATION...
(18Z TAFS)
Issued at 1217 PM CDT Sun Jul 26 2026

Conditions will mainly be VFR with light winds for the next 24 
hours. Patchy fog will lead to MVFR weather for AEX around sunrise
before becoming VFR around 15Z.


&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 1217 PM CDT Sun Jul 26 2026

Light onshore winds and calm seas will continue for the next five
days. Rain chances will return on Thursday.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1217 PM CDT Sun Jul 26 2026

Hot and dry weather will continue well into the work week. Rain
chances will be near zero until Thursday. MinRH will be between 40
and 60 percent through next Friday with RH recovery around 90%.
